text:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert: incident PAGER-8243 triggered for cluster inference-prod. Symptoms: sudden spike in NCCL communicator errors and multi-GPU hangs, repeated container restarts on nodes gpu-12,gpu-13,gpu-17. Error rate > 20% for /v1/generate on model-xlarge-8way. Paging sre oncall now.

sre_jamie: Ack. I'm on it. Can folks paste the latest pod logs for the failing rank? I want the first glimpse of the NCCL stack.

ml_infra_lee: Pasting trimmed log from pod inference-runtime-xyz (rank 2):
```
[2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL WARN  Unhandled cuda error, aborting
[2026-03-15 02:45:21] NCCL ERROR ncclCommAbort called, communicator invalid
[2026-03-15 02:45:21] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
runtime_error: cudaLaunchKernel failed: out of resources
  at /workspace/runtime/collective/comm.c:412
  at /usr/local/bin/inference-runtime
```
We're also seeing container restarts (`CrashLoopBackOff`) and occasional OOMs on the GPU when sequence length spikes.

eng_omar: Likely bad interaction between kernel scheduling and tensor parallel communicator. Could be a race on communicator teardown when a pod gets preempted. Quick mitigation: reduce tensor-parallel degree for active model-route and shift traffic to a smaller single-gpu variant. I'll prepare route change if SRE gives go.

sre_jamie: Immediate mitigation plan (proposed):
1) Temporarily mark the 3 problematic nodes unschedulable (cordon) to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 gpu-13 gpu-17`.
2) Drain the failing pods and restart the runtime on healthy nodes: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl delete pod -l app=inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-12` for each.
3) Apply fallback routing: shift 40% of traffic for model-xlarge-8way to model-xlarge-1gpu (lower throughput, safe single-gpu path).
4) If restarts persist, scale model instances down to TP_SIZE=1/PP_SIZE=1 for the route and restart the deployment.

ml_infra_lee: Executed step 1 & 2 on gpu-12 and gpu-13. Logs show one node had `nvidia-driver` OOM trace and GPU driver process got killed. I cordoned gpu-17 but didn't drain yet (still serving). Sample command I ran:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-12
kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-xyz-2
```

cs_tara: Any idea which customers hit 5xxs? AcmeFinance just flagged errors in prod. Need ETA to share with them.

ml_infra_lee: From metrics: AcmeFinance and BetaRetail were the top two that hit elevated 5xx counts. Total user-facing error rate peaked ~18% on the route. After cordon+drain the error rate dropped to ~6% but still above baseline.

eng_omar: I'm ready to change routing. If SRE confirms the partial reroute, I'll do a canary 20% -> 80% to test stability.

sre_jamie: Do it. eng_omar make it 25/75 for 10 minutes, watch latency and error stream.

deploy-bot: Routing update started by eng_omar: model-xlarge-8way -> 25% traffic to model-xlarge-1gpu. Rollout id: r-20260315-1759

ml_infra_lee: After routing shift we saw error rate go to ~2-3% but latency increased on the single-gpu path as expected. No more NCCL communicator aborts on nodes still serving. Meanwhile, pod restarts have stopped on gpu-12 and gpu-13.

ops_maya: I suggest we also enable NCCL debugging envs on a staging replica to capture more info: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL`. Also consider setting `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` briefly to rule out p2p prob.

sre_jamie: Good call. But don't flood prod logs. Run debug on a single canary pod in a non-customer shard.

ml_infra_lee: Created a debug deployment `inference-debug-canary` with NCCL_DEBUG enabled and TP/PP set to same as prod. Collecting traces now.

sre_jamie: Next steps for live mitigation: keep nodes cordoned, maintain 25/75 routing split, finish draining gpu-17 if safe, and run a controlled rollout with TP_SIZE=1 for model-xlarge across the cluster if we see reoccurrence. Also open a ticket for post-incident capacity adjustments.

cs_tara: Sending a short customer update: "We're investigating elevated errors on model-xlarge; traffic has been partially rerouted to a stable variant and we're working on node restarts. ETA 1h for remediation" — ok to send?

sre_jamie: OK to send. Add note that some customers may see higher latency.

pagerduty: On-call handoff: sre_jamie -> ops_maya at 03:15 UTC. Handoff acknowledged. PagerDuty note: continue mitigation, collect debug logs, and escalate to HW vendor if driver kills persist.

ops_maya: Took over. Running NVIDIA diagnostics on gpu-17 now (`nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,CEC,PERSISTENCE`). One node shows ECC corrected errors increasing.

ml_infra_lee: ECC counts rising on gpu-17, and dmesg shows multiple `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` entries. I queued a maintenance for that host with infra: HOST-REPLACE-178.

eng_omar: Given suspected hardware instability, we should automate fallback routing for high-latency/5xx spikes in future: if error-rate > 5% for 2m, automatically shift 50% traffic to single-gpu variant. Filing an RFC after mitigation.

sre_jamie: Agreed. For now: drained gpu-17 and replaced 2 pods onto healthy nodes. Error rate back to baseline ~0.8%. We'll keep the cluster at reduced TP config overnight and schedule full postmortem.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: r-20260315-1759 -> routing now 10% single-gpu, 90% original (rollback in case of symptoms). All health checks green.

ops_maya: Marking incident as mitigated. Creating a follow-up task: replace gpu-17 host, validate ECC and driver stability, and run a soak test for 6 hours with TP_SIZE=2.

sre_jamie: Closing incident PAGER-8243 as mitigated. Action items: (1) Postmortem + timeline (owner: ml_infra_lee), (2) Auto-fallback RFC (owner: eng_omar), (3) Hardware replacement and soak (owner: ops_maya). I'm adding these to the incident ticket.

cs_tara: Thanks team — will update AcmeFinance and BetaRetail that we've mitigated and will follow up with timeline and RCA.

oncall-bot: Incident PAGER-8243 status -> mitigated. Incident postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC.
